Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat

Interface SendMessageUseCase

All Known Implementing Classes:
SendMessageService
public interface SendMessageUseCase
Use case for POST /conversations/{id}/messages — the only streaming endpoint of the platform (design §7, §16.2).

Returns a cold Flux of TurnEvent: the underlying LLM call is NOT initiated until a subscriber attaches. The REST adapter (US-11-005) is the sole subscriber in production. Calling send(SendMessageCommand) runs a small synchronous prefix — ownership / cap pre-flight and USER message persistence — and ONLY then returns the Flux that emits TurnEvent.Started as its first element.

Synchronous failures (cross-owner, 64-message cap, content drift) propagate as exceptions out of send(SendMessageCommand) itself BEFORE the Flux is returned — they reach the REST adapter via Spring's normal exception path and the global handler writes the matching application/problem+json body (404 / 409 / 400). The SSE stream is never opened in that case.

Reactive failures (LLM timeout, MCP error, agent deleted mid-turn after USER persistence) surface as Flux.error(java.lang.Throwable) — the REST adapter writes the matching error SSE frame after the started frame and closes the emitter.

  • Method Details

    • send

      reactor.core.publisher.Flux<TurnEvent> send(SendMessageUseCase.SendMessageCommand command)
      Runs the chat turn.

      Behavior:

      1. Synchronous prefix: load + verify conversation, check messageCount < 64, persist USER message (transactional), derive title on first message. Throws synchronously on failure; the Flux is never returned in that case.
      2. Reactive tail: emit TurnEvent.Started, build memory window + ChatRequest, stream from the LLM emitting one TurnEvent.Delta per chunk, then on completion persist the ASSISTANT message and emit TurnEvent.Completed.
